_comment: Tool definitions: what each tool is and how to call it. Deliberately not when to call them — that policy is prompts/inject.jinja2, which is injected into every session and is the only place it should live. This file is adjacent to the extension rather than in prompts/ because the extension is its only reader, and sitting next to index.ts guarantees the path resolves however pi loads the module.

remember.promptSnippet: Record a durable observation about the user or project for a future session
description: Record something durable that will still be useful in a future session.
Write it so that someone with no memory of this conversation could act on it.
Include the specifics: the command, the path, the number, the reason behind a
preference, what you got wrong. A memory can never be made more detailed later
than the thought it came from, so detail left out here is lost for good.
Cut the narration. What bloats a thought is the story of what you were doing,
not the facts in it — keep the nouns and the specifics and drop the account of
how you got there. Prefer the general over the anecdote: write the rule about
the recurring task and attach the specifics to it, because a note tied to one
instance never matches a future one.
One observation per call. A thought carrying several unrelated facts can only be
filed as a unit, which makes it harder for the nightly pass to keep what
matters and drop what does not.
Do not judge whether it is worth keeping. A nightly pass filters and files
these, and it can only filter what you recorded.

parameters.thought: The observation, written in full with the specifics — the command, path, number or reason. One observation per call. No date or session id needed; those are added automatically.

recall.promptSnippet: Fetch a memory's full text at full resolution and record that it was used
description: Read one memory at full resolution, and record that it was used.
The list in the Memory section shows each entry at whatever level it has decayed
to, which is often compressed to a handful of keywords. Every entry's full
original text is kept regardless, and this call returns it: a compressed entry
comes back with the specifics that were summarised away — the exact command, the
path, the number, the reason. The call returns at least what the list line shows,
and for a decayed entry it returns substantially more.
It also adds one to the entry's cumulative evidence count. That count never goes
down: it decides which entries are compressed when the store runs out of room,
and which eventually become permanent.
An id that is not in the list returns an error rather than a guess, so an id
that looks subtly wrong is worth re-reading from the list before calling.

parameters.memory_id: Id of the memory to recall, exactly as it appears in the list, e.g. "m3f". Without brackets.
